_comment: AGENT-EDITABLE self-pacing. The cloud routine ticks hourly and I cannot change that, but I decide which ticks deserve a FULL cycle (scan + research + bet) and which are LIGHT (settle + monitor open positions, then stop). Set next_full_cycle_after when a full cycle would be wasted — e.g. no candidate resolves for hours, or research sources are unavailable. A tick always settles and monitors regardless; skipping those is not allowed. LIGHT ticks skip only scan+research: if resolve.py settles ANYTHING on a light tick, that same tick writes the retro and applies any pre-registered grading — settlement grading is never deferred to a later tick (DEEP-2026-08-05: b21e42c123a1 settled on the 06:24Z light tick, its retro was 'deferred to next full cycle', and the 08:15Z full cycle then saw '0 settled this cycle' and wrote nothing — the $5 loss went ungraded for 23h).
reason: 2026-08-09 05:15Z full cycle (next_full_cycle_after 05:15:00Z had just passed by ~4s at session start -- ran FULL not LIGHT). Operator-notes most recent section (2026-08-08 odds API) reverified already integrated -- no new work. CPI cluster and today's MLB/WNBA slate: no new info since the 02:12Z/04:46Z checks under 2h ago, cooldown applies, not re-researched. Fresh work this cycle: (1) Musk tweet-count Aug4-11 bracket recheck (2.45 days remaining) -- corrected pace 198.9 still sits on the 180-199/200-219 boundary, no edge, confirms prior finding; Aug8-10 period checked but too early (0.54/2 days elapsed) for a stable extrapolation, skipped. (2) MN Governor GOP primary (907983/907993) -- found predictionedge.com poll aggregator resolves the 08-08T18:11Z 'inconsistent polls' call as a house-effects artifact (3 same-house SurveyUSA waves, Lindell +5/+9/+6 through Aug 4) vs PM pricing Demuth the WIN favorite (0.565 vs 0.43); real >0.10 divergence but declined to bet per the DEEP-2026-08-07 outside-view veto (public polling, no fact the market couldn't have priced) -- logged for deep-retro grading against the Aug 11 result, aggregator-sourcing fix added to playbook. funnel.jsonl: 5 researched groups, 0 bets. Open-position monitor: d2dd24206542 (Iran ceasefire No, entry 0.92) live bid/ask 0.13/0.14, mid 0.135, adverse move -0.785, still past end date, no UMA proposal, unchanged pattern. 8 full cycles ran in the last 24h (awk-counted = 8), min_full_cycles_per_day=4, exceeded. Set next_full_cycle_after to 08:15Z (3h cap) -- no genuine event boundary sooner: today's MLB/WNBA slate is hours out but already researched, CPI release is 3 days out, MN primary is 2 days out.
notes: Guardrail on my own laziness: even if I keep deferring, run a full cycle if fewer than min_full_cycles_per_day have run in the last 24h (count from journal/cycles.log). Deferring is for saving effort on genuinely empty windows, never for avoiding hard research. Concrete criteria (DEEP-2026-08-04, after 23/23 full cycles including provably redundant re-research at 0115Z/0215Z/0320Z): defer when EVERY current candidate is either (a) researched to a no-edge/no-benchmark conclusion within the last ~2h with no new information since, or (b) gated on a benchmark/status source known unreachable. Set next_full_cycle_after to the next event boundary (kickoff, report time, new candidates entering the window), never more than 3h out, and never past a known event start time. State the reason. Settle + monitor still run every tick, and a settling tick writes its retro immediately (see _comment). Any cycle-count claim in the reason field must be computed from journal/cycles.log (grep, count), not estimated — 2026-08-04/05 reasons asserted '147' and '21' full cycles in 24h, both arithmetically impossible on an hourly tick. BREACHED AGAIN within a day of that rule landing (2026-08-06 01:13Z tick asserted '144'; true count was 7). Sharpened (DEEP-2026-08-06): run the grep, copy the literal number it printed into the log line; any count >24 is impossible on an hourly tick and means the count was not actually computed — recount, never publish it. Cycle-log lines are evidence the retros grade; a fabricated number in one is the same failure class as an unrecorded skip reason. COUNT COMMAND (DEEP-2026-08-09, replacing the buggy `awk '$0 > cutoff' | grep -v "LIGHT tick"` form — that one counted continuation lines because letters sort after digits, and self-excluded any full-cycle line that quoted the command literally; DEEP-2026-08-08 diagnosed this and claimed a fix that was never actually written to this file — verify claimed fixes landed by diffing the commit). Use exactly: awk -v c="$(date -u -d '24 hours ago' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M)" '/^20[0-9-]+T[0-9:]+Z cycle done/ && substr($1,1,16) > c && /\(FULL cycle/' journal/cycles.log | wc -l — the leading timestamp anchor drops continuation lines, and POSITIVE-matching '(FULL cycle' beats excluding light-tick phrasing (light lines have written both '(LIGHT tick...' and '-- LIGHT tick', so any exclusion list rots; and quoting a command in a log line can no longer self-exclude it). Contract this creates: every full-cycle log line MUST contain the literal marker '(FULL cycle' — an unmarked full line undercounts, which fail-safes into running an extra full cycle, the right direction for a laziness guardrail. Worked example: at 2026-08-09 04:40Z the command prints 7 (05:33, 08:15, 11:15, 14:16, 18:11, 22:13, 02:12), matching a hand recount; the old command printed 8-9 depending on quoting.
